historical_references.reference:
Mulail ibn Rabi'ah al-Muradi, a prominent scholar and jurist in the Maliki school of Islamic law during the 11th and 12th centuries. He was born in Murad, near Tunis, and studied under the renowned scholar Ibn Hazm of Cordoba. Mulail became a judge in Seville, Spain, and later served as a judge and chief qadi in Almeria, Granada, and Valencia. He was known for his rigorous adherence to Maliki doctrine and his ability to reconcile the various schools of Islamic law.
Time period: 11th - 12th centuries
Context: Maliki scholar and jurist

Mulail ibn Said al-Din, a 14th century Syrian scholar and theologian who was a prominent figure in the Mamluk period. He was a Hanafi scholar and a prominent student of Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya. Mulail wrote extensively on Islamic theology, philosophy, and jurisprudence. He was known for his position on the issue of the pre-existence of the Quran, which was controversial at the time. He argued that the Quran did not have a pre-existent existence, but was created in time with the speech of Allah.
Time period: 14th century
Context: Hanafi scholar and theologian
